kinds.d: Fossilised tree resin, raw, polished or cut, with or without insects or other inclusions; organised by deposit.

x.d: Eocene amber (succinite, 3–8% succinic acid) from the Prussian Formation; over 90% of the world's amber comes from Kaliningrad Oblast, and it has been traded since the Neolithic.
x.dt: insects over 98% of animal inclusions · mosses and liverworts · feathers and reptiles rare

x.d: Almost always transparent amber from the Dominican Republic, with rare fluorescent blue amber reported mostly from Palo Quemado, and many ant, termite and plant inclusions.
x.dt: Cordillera Septentrional, Bayaguana, Sabana de la Mar · Miocene to about 40 Ma estimates · blue fluorescence

x.d: Mid-Cretaceous amber (about 100 million years old) from the Hukawng Valley, Kachin State, Myanmar, with rich arthropod and some vertebrate inclusions; ethics concerns over conflict funding.

v.n: Society of Vertebrate Paleontology moratorium proposal
v.d: Proposed no publication on specimens bought from Myanmar sources after June 2017

x.dt: Tengchong main market · Myitkyina trade · ethical provenance issues

x.d: Miocene amber from Simojovel and other Chiapas mines, protected designation of origin, comparable in quality to Dominican amber; Mexican law recognises 17 colourations.
x.dt: Simojovel produces about 95% · white to red, green, blue, black

x.d: Early Cretaceous amber (about 130–125 million years ago) from the Grès du Liban, the oldest amber with a significant number of inclusions.
Pressed amber (ambroid) made by heating and compressing fragments; also copal, kauri gum, celluloid, Bakelite and acrylic fakes.
x.dt: pressed amber shows interference colours in polarised light · tests: infrared spectroscopy

kinds.d: Young, partly fossilised tree resin, sold beside amber.

x.d: Subfossil copal found in Colombia, Madagascar, Japan and the Dominican Republic, often with insect inclusions.
x.dt: lighter citrine colour than amber · acetone or chloroform makes the surface tacky

x.d: Well-known subfossil copal from the New Zealand kauri Agathis australis.
Subfossil resin of Hymenaea verrucosa from East Africa, lying one or two metres below living trees.

kinds.d: Fossil insect or other land arthropod preserved in rock. An insect in amber or copal is under Amber or Copal.

x.d: Compression fossils in limestone from the Aptian Crato Formation, Brazil (about 113 million years ago), with abundant dragonflies and damselflies.
x.dt: limestone nodules and slabs · soft tissue preserved · illegal trade concerns

x.d: Often complete insects preserved in the Eocene Green River Formation of Wyoming.

notes: Inclusion types are detail axes (dt) in Amber. Lebanese amber age differs inside the Wikipedia article (Hauterivian vs Barremian), so given as Early Cretaceous. Green River shrimp and Colombian/Madagascan copal specifics (only the list of localities) are minimal. Insect-in-amber inclusions are not separate kinds.
